**1.** Model Diagnostics.

**(a)** (10 pt) For each of the five scenarios below, identify: (i) which assumption is violated, and (ii) the appropriate remedial action. 

| Scenario | Diagnostic plot | What you see |
|:--------:|:----------------|:-------------|
| 1 | Residuals vs. fitted $\hat{Y}$ | Residuals fan out as $\hat{Y}$ increases |
| 2 | Residuals vs. $X$ | A curved U-shape where residuals are negative at the ends, positive in the middle |
| 3 | Residuals vs. time order | Residuals alternate in a cyclical pattern |
| 4 | Normal QQ-plot | Points follow the line in the middle but curve upward sharply at both ends (heavy tails) |
| 5 | Residuals vs. fitted $\hat{Y}$ | Points are randomly scattered around zero with no pattern |

**3.** Introduction to Multiple Regression.

**(a)** (8 pt) For each model below, state whether it is a **general linear model**. Justify each answer in one sentence by identifying whether every $\beta$ parameter enters the model **linearly** (linear in the parameters, not necessarily in the predictors).

$$\text{(i)}\quad Y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_1 + \beta_2 X_1^2 + \beta_3 X_2 + \epsilon$$

$$\text{(ii)}\quad Y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_1^{\,\beta_2} + \epsilon$$

$$\text{(iii)}\quad Y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \log(X_1) + \beta_2 X_1 X_2 + \epsilon$$

$$\text{(iv)}\quad Y = \frac{\beta_0 + \beta_1 X_1}{1 + \beta_2 X_2} + \epsilon$$
